q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Net sales did not drop — they rose sharply on 2026-10-13 to ₹91,220 from ₹40,119 on 2026-10-12 (+127%). In short: sales increased, driven by more orders and a higher average order value, especially on Meta.

- What moved (size): Net sales ₹40,119 → ₹91,220 (+127%). Orders 26 → 45 (+73%) and Net AOV ₹1,543 → ₹2,027 (+31%). Together, orders explain ≈66% of the sales lift and higher AOV ≈34%.
- Biggest contributor by channel: Meta rose from ₹6,290 → ₹47,854 and accounts for the single largest platform share of the change; Google rose modestly (₹11,847 → ₹16,862).
- What changed inside the order mix: units sold increased 27 → 61 (+126%); units per order and AOV both rose (units/order 1.04 → 1.36, AOV ₹2,116 → ₹2,694), so more items and higher-priced baskets.
- Data notes & confidence: period totals and the component split are exact; daily values overlap a lot (normal day-to-day variation). A few tax-series failed to fetch but that does not change the net sales result.

Worth checking: drill to Meta campaigns/ads that spiked (the diagnosis flagged specific ads and a few shipping-state sales increases).
